for: l1_background_level_perframe_vs_onstack — the one held-fixed item the pre-registration does not pin: the per-group `register -2pass` reference INSIDE each member build
question: does `--subsky-lights` move the reference frame `register -2pass` picks, and is that pick stable under identical input?
why_it_matters: the 2pass chooses its reference from image QUALITY, and subtracting a plane per frame changes every frame's statistics. A different reference gives a different -framing=min member canvas, which covers different sky, which lands different lattice cells `used` — and the PAIRED retained fraction (5-16% resolving power) is computed over the cells both arms share. Losing the pairing costs the experiment its sensitivity, dropping it toward the 43-55% an absolute slope resolves.
design: ONE KNOB (--subsky-lights) through the production builder run_undistort_pipeline.sh, 12 CONSECUTIVE frames (the first 12 of the control's own sessions/aug06/work/groups_set-01/g1.list, so the geometry is a real member's, not an even stride), --chunk=12, same master dark and per-set sky flat, same pinned optical model, --regdata= pointed at a NON-EXISTENT path so each arm SAVES its registration data instead of pinning it. Plus a REPEAT of the unflagged arm, identical in every argument, as the determinism control.
instrument: Siril's own registration data (the `.seq` it writes: reference_image is field 6 of the S line, the per-image homographies are the R rows) and the delivered stack's NAXIS1/NAXIS2. No in-house measurement.
result: THE REFERENCE MOVES ON THE KNOB: index 8 -> 11, and the canvas 6038x4033 -> 6037x4030 (1 px in x, 3 px in y at 12 frames' drift; the production member spans 100 frames). AND THE PICK IS DETERMINISTIC: the repeat's .seq is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the first arm's (same reference, same homographies) and its stack is PIXEL-IDENTICAL — 0 differing of 73,053,762, the only header differences being DATE and the REGPIN filename. So the movement is caused by the calibration change, not by run-to-run jitter, and `register -2pass` is a deterministic function of its input on this rig.
decision: PIN. Step 2 of the brief applies, and determinism makes it exactly executable: because the registration is a deterministic function of the frames, re-running the UNFLAGGED arm reproduces the control's own registration, so the donor is not a stand-in for the control's registration data — it IS it, verifiable by the rebuilt members reproducing the control's members pixel-for-pixel. `--regdata-dir=` plumbed through run_undistort_groups.sh (one gNN.seq per group; first arm writes, later arms read); arm A pinned to a donor arm rebuilt from the control's own configuration.
cost_of_not_pinning: arm A would differ from the control by TWO knobs — the background step and a re-chosen registration reference per member — inside an experiment whose whole design is one knob.
scope: aug06/set-01, 12 consecutive frames, Siril 1.4.4 flatpak on this rig. The direction (a calibration change re-ranks the reference) replicates the flat-differential session's measurement of the same mechanism on aug09/set-05 with the FLAT as the knob (image 1 / 4896x3616 against image 2 / 4887x3641).
surfaces: sessions/aug06/work/l1_pilot/ (stacks + siril logs, gitignored); the .seq donors and this record under datasets/aug06/set-01/l1_work/
